Construct strict Bayes factor evidence regions

singlearm_bf_regions.Rd

Classifies Bayes factors into an efficacy region and, optionally, a region of compelling evidence for H0 and an inconclusive region.

Usage

singlearm_bf_regions(bfvals, k, k_ce = NULL)

Arguments

bfvals

Numeric vector of nonnegative Bayes factors BF01 comparing H0 with H1, without missing values. Zero and positive infinity are permitted.

k

Positive finite efficacy threshold on BF01. Efficacy is defined by the strict inequality \(BF_{01}<k\).

k_ce

Optional positive finite threshold greater than k. Compelling evidence for H0 is defined by the strict inequality \(BF_{01}>k_{\mathrm{ce}}\). If NULL, only efficacy and its complement are returned.

Value

A named list of logical vectors, each with the same length as bfvals. If k_ce = NULL, the components are:

efficacy

Whether \(BF_{01}<k\).

not_efficacy

Whether \(BF_{01}\ge k\).

Otherwise, the components are:

efficacy

Whether \(BF_{01}<k\).

compelling_h0

Whether \(BF_{01}>k_{\mathrm{ce}}\).

inconclusive

Whether \(k \le BF_{01} \le k_{\mathrm{ce}}\).

Details

When k_ce is supplied, the regions are mutually exclusive and exhaustive. Values equal to either threshold are classified as inconclusive: \(k \le BF_{01} \le k_{\mathrm{ce}}\).

When k_ce = NULL, not_efficacy denotes the complement of efficacy, \(BF_{01}\ge k\). It should not be interpreted as compelling evidence for H0.

The usual evidential interpretation uses \(0<k<1<k_{\mathrm{ce}}\), although the function only requires k > 0 and, when supplied, k_ce > k.

Comparisons are applied directly to the supplied floating-point values without an explicit numerical tolerance.
